Temporary carbon storage can mitigate slow-responding climate changes
articles.abstract: Abstract Carbon removal and storage is central to many net-zero commitments, yet its durability, particularly for nature-based methods, is uncertain due to disturbance risks. Previous work shows that carbon storage-years (the time-integrated quantity of carbon storage) are proportional to time-integrated avoided warming, which in turn causes avoided changes in slow-responding climate variables. Here, we show that temporary carbon storage results in avoided changes in inertial climate variables. Avoided changes in 2100 are proportional to carbon storage-years across a range of storage amounts and emissions scenarios for permafrost carbon, ocean carbon, Atlantic meridional overturning circulation, ocean temperature, and thermosteric sea-level rise. By 2300, proportionality persists in some variables, notably sea-level rise, ocean temperature, and ocean carbon. Temporary storage therefore has climate benefits that extend beyond the duration of the storage, with some persistence of benefits even on multi-century timescales. We find that these climate benefits are greatest when temporary storage is paired with ambitious mitigation.

Hypertensive stress rewires macrophage signaling in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction independent of obesity
articles.abstract: Abstract Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) remains a major unmet clinical challenge. Although obesity is common in many HFpEF cohorts from Europe and North America, three Japanese HFpEF cohorts identified hypertension and sympathetic overactivation, rather than obesity, as dominant features. To model these features, we established an HFpEF mouse model in which sympathetic activation induces hypertensive heart disease, while endothelial dysfunction acts as a second hit driving progression to HFpEF. Hypertensive stress rewires cardiac macrophage-derived intercellular signaling, impairing macrophage-to-cardiomyocyte BMP signaling and fatty acid oxidation while enhancing macrophage-to-fibroblast PDGF signaling, thereby promoting metabolic remodeling, inflammation, and fibrosis. ANGPTL2 inhibition preserves macrophage intercellular communication and prevents HFpEF development. These findings identify cardiac macrophage signaling rewiring as a central mechanism linking hypertensive stress to metabolic remodeling and inflammation, revealing a pathogenic pathway for HFpEF in the absence of obesity that is distinct from HFpEF associated with obesity.

articles.title: Cobalt-catalyzed alkyne migratory hydroboration to access β-alkenylboronates via catalytic zipper-like alkyne translocation
Hydroxy artificial water channels enable ultraselective reverse osmosis membranes for N-nitrosamine removal in water reuse
Infant hippocampal and amygdala volume in an observational follow-up from a randomized clinical trial for maternal prenatal depression
articles.abstract: Abstract Prenatal maternal depression may have intergenerational effects on offspring brain development, with potential socioemotional consequences. This observational follow-up study examines brain development and subsequent negative emotionality among 109 infants born to mothers participating in a randomized clinical trial (NCT03011801). In the prior trial, brief interpersonal psychotherapy significantly reduced prenatal depression symptoms and disorder as the published primary and secondary endpoints. Exploratory infant outcomes include hippocampal and amygdala volumes at 6 weeks and negative emotionality at 6 months. Here we show that infants of mothers randomized to interpersonal psychotherapy during pregnancy have lower right hippocampal volume than infants of mothers in the enhanced usual care group ( p = .002, d = 0.62). No statistically significant group differences are observed in left hippocampal or amygdala volume. Smaller hippocampal volume predicts subsequent lower negative emotionality (r = 0.19, p = 0.045). In this study, a maternal prenatal depression intervention is associated with differences in infant brain development with implications for their subsequent emotional health.

articles.title: 3D confinement physically regulates cell cycle progression in budding yeast

The molecular heterogeneity and clinical impact of genomic driver alterations in prostate cancer
Market Integration Pathways for Enhanced Geothermal Systems in Europe
articles.abstract: Abstract Enhanced geothermal systems can provide constant, reliable electricity and heat with minimal emissions, but high drilling costs and uncertain cost reductions leave their future unclear. We explore scenarios for the future adoption of these systems in a carbon-neutral, multi-sector European energy system. Here we show that in a net-zero system, heat (co-)generating enhanced geothermal plants at current cost can support 20–30 gigawatts (GW) of thermal capacity in Europe, primarily driven by district heating demands. If drilling costs were to decrease by approximately 60% relative to 2020 costs, the technology would become competitive in electricity markets, greatly expanding its market opportunity. However, the spatially dispersed rollout of district heating stands against the confined overlap of high geological potential with low potential for other renewables, which conditions the competitiveness of electricity-generating plants. This results in a challenge where the majority of the market potential depends on pan-European technology learning for cost reductions, emphasising that coordination is crucial in stakeholders’ efforts.

articles.title: From fragmentation to fault zone architecture as a structural framework for fault weakening
Structural basis for loop-dependent inhibition by AcrIIC1 anti-CRISPR proteins
Coordinated inhibition of SOX9 and cell-cycle progression by microRNA-200 restricts sebaceous gland fate specification
articles.abstract: Abstract The microRNA-200 family (miR-200s) is known for inhibiting epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition and cell-cycle progression in cancer, but its function in epithelial development remains unclear. Here we show that miR-200s are highly enriched in hair matrix progenitors but absent from the upper hair follicle (HF), where sebaceous gland (SG) and HF stem cells are specified. Ectopic miR-200 induction abolishes SG specification while preserving hair morphogenesis. Genome-wide identification of miR-200 targets reveals direct repression of negative regulators of WNT signaling and cell-cycle regulators. Single-cell and spatial transcriptomic analyses uncover mutually exclusive domains of WNT activity and SOX9 expression in the upper HF that is disrupted by miR-200 induction. Genome-wide mapping of SOX9 targets further uncovers a lipogenic and fatty-acid metabolic program required for SG specification. Together, these findings show that miR-200 blocks SG fate by inhibiting SOX9 function and restricting cell proliferation, defining a spatially organized regulatory network essential for SG development.

articles.title: Medium-Entropy LDH-Driven Electronic Coupling of MnO x for Preferential Oxidation of Formaldehyde
articles.abstract: Abstract Preferential oxidation of formaldehyde (HCHO) in natural gas engine exhaust is pivotal to prevent NH3–SCR catalyst deactivation and inhibit highly toxic hydrogen cyanide (HCN) formation. Although manganese-based catalysts exhibit prominent activity for HCHO oxidation, complete mineralization is still hindered by poor electron-transfer efficiency and insufficient reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation. Herein, we fabricate hierarchical medium-entropy LDH nanoflower-anchored MnOx catalysts (MnO2@NiMgAl-MELH) via a facile in situ growth strategy, enabling 100% mineralization of HCHO at room temperature. Structural characterizations and DFT calculations verify that Ni–Mn electronic coupling optimizes the electronic structure, facilitates charge transfer, reduces oxygen vacancy formation energy, and boosts O2 and H2O activation to generate abundant ROS (O2–, O22–, and surface −OH). Furthermore, in situ DRIFTS confirms that ROS synergistically accelerate HCHO and formate intermediate oxidation, achieving complete mineralization of HCHO. This work develops a low-cost and high-performance catalyst for HCHO preferential oxidation and offers a broadly applicable strategy for air pollutant purification.

articles.title:
Bromine Monoxide
Radical Likely Dominates Dimethylsulfide
Oxidation before the Springtime Onset of Arctic Ice Melt
articles.abstract: Abstract To understand the atmospheric fate of dimethylsulfide (DMS) during the Arctic spring-to-summer transition, we measured volatile methylated sulfur (VMS) species, including DMS and DMS-derived oxidation products, dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO), and dimethylsulfone (DMSO2), in the Fram Strait during May and June of 2023. Elevated DMSO contributions to VMS accompany depleted O3, high surface albedo, and air temperatures < 0 °C in air masses influenced by snow-covered sea-ice regions, suggesting that BrO•-initiated oxidation dominated DMS loss prior to the onset of sea-ice melt. In GEOS-Chem simulations, BrO• is the dominant oxidant for DMS, but modeled BrO• concentrations from sea-salt debromination alone are too low to replicate observed O3, DMSO, and DMSO2, suggesting a missing source of reactive bromine from sunlit saline snow. BrO•-initiated oxidation reduces the DMS lifetime and oxidizes DMS through methanesulfinic acid (MSIA) more quickly in the gas phase and in higher yields compared to •OH-initiated oxidation alone. Once melt onset begins and snowpack-driven halogen activation shuts off, •OH oxidation likely dominates Arctic DMS oxidation. Our observations highlight the seasonal variability of halogen oxidation impacting sulfur species in the Arctic marine region, which are likely to change as the sea-ice extent decreases and the melt season in the Arctic lengthens.

articles.title:
Atmospheric
Removal
of Nitrous Oxide: Approaches and
Feasibility
articles.abstract: Abstract Nitrous oxide (N2O) is the third-largest contributor to anthropogenic greenhouse gas forcing and the dominant anthropogenic ozone-depleting emission. While mitigation can flatten emissions, there is no clear pathway to eliminate residual emissions from agriculture and other diffuse sources, a key challenge for climate stabilization. The potential role of atmospheric removal has not been holistically assessed, yet N2O’s high potency and long atmospheric lifetime indicate the potential for a durable climate benefit. This review synthesizes emerging approaches for atmospheric N2O removal, organized by reaction mechanism (thermal destruction and thermocatalysis, photolysis, gas-phase radical reactions, photocatalysis, and biological reduction) and deployment format (closed versus open system). Each is evaluated for technical efficacy, climate viability, environmental and social viability, and economic plausibility using lower-bound cost models. No approach yet satisfies all four: gas-phase radical reactors are precluded by their kinetics, thermocatalytic and photocatalytic reactors require ten- to hundred-fold performance gains, and open-system approaches have the lowest cost floors but face the greatest measurement and governance challenges. These results identify the performance thresholds and broader constraints that govern feasibility across pathways, providing a foundation for a research agenda and for assessing the role of N2O removal alongside emissions mitigation.

articles.title:
Toward Rational
Design of Low-Salt-Rejection Reverse
Osmosis for Minimal and Zero Liquid Discharge
articles.abstract: Abstract Low-salt-rejection reverse osmosis (LSRRO) has emerged as a promising technology for concentrating high-salinity brines in minimal- and zero-liquid-discharge (MLD/ZLD) applications. However, rational LSRRO design remains hindered by uncertainties about how existing modeling frameworks should be interpreted and applied. In this Perspective, we critically examine the limitations of process modeling and module-scale analysis in LSRRO design. Conventional process models can yield misleading predictions for spiral-wound LSRRO modules because the stagewise concentration cutoff embedded in these models is based on the cumulative permeate composition rather than the local permeate conditions that govern water transport. Experimental results and local transport calculations show that the brine concentration in spiral-wound LSRRO stages is not constrained by a fixed thermodynamic concentration cutoff. Nevertheless, standalone process models remain inherently limited in assessing practical feasibility because they do not resolve kinetic constraints, such as declining water flux along the module. Module-scale analysis is therefore essential for linking local transport behavior to practical design metrics, including membrane area requirements, productivity, and achievable brine concentration. However, its predictive accuracy is constrained because transport parameters derived from conventional local transport models vary with salinity, which challenges their use as constants across the module. This Perspective therefore highlights the need for condition-dependent and experimentally validated local transport descriptions to enable rational LSRRO design for future MLD/ZLD applications.

articles.title:
Sex-Specific
Associations of Gestational OPE Exposure
with Offspring Digit Ratio: A Birth Cohort Study
articles.abstract: Abstract The effect of prenatal organophosphate esters (OPEs) exposure on offspring reproductive development and the potential role of the placenta remain unclear. We investigated the associations of prenatal OPE exposure with the second-to-fourth digit ratio (2D:4D) and the mediating role of placental DNA methylation (DNAm) levels of PPAR pathway genes. Maternal urine OPE metabolites at 12–16 gestational weeks were measured. Placental DNAm levels at birth and children’s 2D:4D at ages 4 and 6 years were assessed. Multiple linear regression, BKMR, and causal mediation analyses were applied. We observed associations between prenatal exposure to BBOEP, BEHP, DBP, and DPP and increased 2D:4D in boys, whereas DBP and DCP were associated with decreased 2D:4D in girls. BKMR identified alkyl-OPEs, particularly BBOEP, as the primary contributors in boys. Moreover, hypermethylation of RXRA, ACAA1, and ACADM was associated with decreased 2D:4D in all populations. In girls, the associations among higher OPE exposure, increased ACAA1 methylation, and lower 2D:4D suggested a potential mediation pathway, while the mediation effects were not statistically significant. These findings suggest sex-specific associations between prenatal OPE exposure and 2D:4D. The potential role of placental PPAR-related DNAm in these associations warrants further investigation.

articles.title:
Dynamic Nature of
Soil Iron Minerals: Recent Advances
Using Iron Isotope Tracers and Mössbauer Spectroscopy
articles.abstract: Abstract Iron plays a central role in defining the redox and surface chemical environment of soils and sediments, by mediating the behavior of nutrients, pollutants, and carbon compounds. However, the mechanisms that drive dynamic changes in Fe speciation and mineral composition can be difficult to trace. Over three decades, technical advances in spectroscopy and theoretical modeling techniques have revealed detailed mechanisms of Fe mineral recrystallization and transformation. Here, we provide a perspective on the application of iron isotopic tracers to the development of atomic-scale mechanistic understanding of Fe mineral dynamics. We review key milestones in the advancement of 57Fe tracers coupled with 57Fe Mössbauer spectroscopy and draw links between the understanding of Fe dynamics with 57Fe tracers and biogeochemical cycling of other elements in soils and sediments. Iron isotopes are increasingly used in Fe biogeochemistry research, and our analysis will point out unique opportunities offered by 57Fe tracers to unravel important questions in soil biogeochemistry today.

articles.title:
Unveiling Whole
Water Neurotoxicity through Sensitive
Electrophysiological Functional Profiling: Beyond Conventional Morphological
Metrics
articles.abstract: Abstract Neuroactive contaminants typically coexist as complex mixtures in aquatic ecosystems, exerting deleterious effects through combined exposures. However, current assessment approaches based on morphological endpoints (e.g., neurite outgrowth) lack sufficient sensitivity to capture functional neurotoxicity of these mixtures. To address this gap, this study establishes in vitro functional neurotoxicity testing (iFNT), an ultrasensitive bioassay leveraging high-density microelectrode arrays to profile cortical network electrophysiology. Validated using reference toxicants, their mixture, and whole water samples, iFNT achieves 5- to 500-fold higher sensitivity than the neurite outgrowth assay. This heightened sensitivity enables clearer discrimination of functional phenotypes for both individual compounds at environmentally relevant concentrations (10–8 M) and whole water samples without preconcentration, providing a powerful tool for evaluating real-world neurotoxic risks. Alarmingly, conventional monitoring indicators exhibited a pronounced mismatch with iFNT profiles across wastewater treatment stages, demonstrating that seemingly acceptable routine readings masked the persistence of latent neurotoxicity. This study challenges morphology-based paradigms, revealing that accurate whole water risk assessment necessitates integrating functional biological endpoints into future monitoring frameworks.

articles.title: Microscale spatial fragmentation promotes bacterial survival under antibiotics
USP28 potentiates endothelial necroptosis via deubiquitinating NMMHC IIA in septic male mice
articles.abstract: Abstract Endothelial dysfunction contributes to multi-organ injury in sepsis, but the underlying mechanisms remain incompletely understood. Here we show that endothelial ubiquitin-specific protease 28 (USP28) is increased in patients with sepsis and in male mice in a murine polymicrobial sepsis model. Mechanistically, USP28 stabilizes non-muscle myosin heavy chain IIA (NMMHC IIA) by removing K48-linked ubiquitination at K1413. Moreover, NMMHC IIA promotes interferon-α/β receptor 1 (IFNAR1) trafficking to the plasma membrane, enhancing IFNAR1/signal transducer and activator of transcription 1 (STAT1) signaling and endothelial necroptosis. In turn, STAT1 transcriptionally increases USP28 expression, forming a positive feedback loop. Endothelial USP28 deletion or pharmacological inhibition attenuates sepsis-induced multi-organ injury, whereas USP28 overexpression exacerbates it. Conversely, endothelial NMMHC IIA or IFNAR1 overexpression largely abrogates the protection conferred by USP28 deficiency in septic male mice. These findings identify a USP28–NMMHC IIA axis that promotes endothelial necroptosis and multi-organ injury in sepsis through IFNAR1/STAT1 signaling.

articles.title: Thromboxane A2 receptor signalling amplifies osteoclastogenesis in rheumatoid arthritis through ACSL1 associated mitochondrial oxidative metabolism
Archean subduction-derived noble gases in the lithospheric mantle beneath the São Francisco Craton
Coupling hfCas13d with Circular gRNA Array Precursors Extends RNA Knockdown and Improves Biocatalysis in Yeast

A Unified Quantitative
Framework for Assessing Uncertainty
in Microbial-Explicit Soil Carbon Models under Diverse Data Availability
of Field Observations
articles.abstract: Abstract Microbial-explicit soil carbon models offer mechanistic representations of soil carbon turnover, but their application to the field remains limited, which is commonly attributed to the scarce microbial observations. However, usually there are significant mismatches between model data requirements and the diverse data availability of field observations, which may greatly affect the uncertainty of soil carbon models and have been largely overlooked. Here, we developed a unified framework that systematically quantified how the field observation type, sampling frequency, and measurement uncertainty jointly constrained model parameters and long-term predictions of three representative microbial-explicit soil carbon models. We quantified how well observations of soil carbon stocks, soil respiration, microbial biomass carbon, and functional gene abundance can reduce the parameter and prediction uncertainties across a comprehensive set of field scenarios. High-frequency, low-error soil respiration observations, when combined with soil carbon measurements, dominated uncertainty reduction across carbon pools, while interestingly, microbial observations only provided conditional improvements for microbial and enzyme-related states. More microbial data did not necessarily yield more effective calibration information, and improvements in prediction accuracy required microbial observations with sufficiently small measurement errors. The unified quantitative framework would also help to design a data strategy when developing new soil carbon models to accurately predict soil carbon cycling.

articles.title: Efficient Water Resistance via High-Spin-State Manganese Species in Low-Temperature NH 3 -SCR
articles.abstract: Abstract Development of highly efficient catalysts for low-temperature NH3–SCR remains a significant challenge, especially in the presence of high concentrations of water vapor. Herein, we have engineered a unique MnCeO2-TDA catalyst with high-spin manganese species by using electron-donating thiophene groups, achieving an excellent NO conversion of over 93% at 160 °C and under 60,000 mL·g–1·h–1 conditions in the higher water vapor of 10–20 vol %. Experimental and theoretical calculations demonstrate that, due to, asymmetrically occupied eg orbitals, high-spin Mn3+ triggers a strong Jahn–Teller distortion, which greatly decreases the O2 dissociation energy (from 2.837 to 1.979 eV) and coactivates O2 and H2O to form the *OOH oxidative species. This enhanced redox ability facilitates NO oxidation and the “fast SCR” reaction, leading to excellent deNOx efficiency under higher levels of water vapor at low temperatures. This work offers a new approach to modulating the spin state of active centers to enhance water resistance in flue gas purification.

articles.title:
PFAS
in Follicular Fluid, Anti-Müllerian Hormone,
and Oocyte Developmental Competence: A Prospective Study in GIVES
articles.abstract: Abstract In this prospective study based on the Guangxi In Vitro Fertilization and the Environment Study (GIVES) cohort, we measured poly- and perfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) in the ovarian follicular fluid of 729 participants to investigate their association with oocyte developmental competence. The PFAS mixture was negatively associated with Metaphase II (MII) oocyte rate, with chlorinated polyfluoroalkyl ether sulfonic acids (Cl-PFESAs) identified as the primary contributor in Bayesian kernel machine regression (BKMR) models. Cl-PFESAs were negatively associated with oocyte maturation [relative risk (RR) = 0.67, 95% CI: 0.56–0.79], fertilization (RR = 0.78, 95% CI: 0.67–0.90), blastocyst formation (RR = 0.81, 95% CI: 0.70–0.94), and high-quality blastocyst formation (RR = 0.49, 95% CI: 0.41–0.58). Serum anti-Müllerian hormone (AMH) may act as a key modifier, with a stronger association observed in women with low AMH for MII oocyte rate [relative excess risk due to interaction (RERI) = 0.33, 95% CI: 0.12–0.54] and fertilization rate (RERI = 0.24, 95% CI: 0.003–0.49). Our findings indicate that PFAS, particularly Cl-PFESAs, in follicular fluid are linked to impaired oocyte developmental competence, with AMH serving as a potential modifier. Further studies are warranted to validate our findings and assess the implications of PFAS for reproductive outcomes.

articles.title:
Trimester-Specific
Associations of Prenatal Heat Exposure
with Neonatal Amino Acid and Acylcarnitine Profiles
articles.abstract: Abstract It remains unclear whether prenatal heat exposure is associated with newborn metabolic profiles. Therefore, based on 4714 mother–infant pairs in Shanghai, we aimed to investigate the trimester-specific associations of prenatal heat exposure with neonatal amino acid (AA) and acylcarnitine (AC) profiles. Heat exposure was defined using the 90th percentile of trimester-specific temperature distributions from the ERA5-Land data set. For AAs, glutamate showed consistently positive associations across three trimesters, whereas phenylalanine, tyrosine, leucine, arginine, and citrulline showed consistently negative associations; other AAs exhibited trimester-specific patterns. For ACs, C2, C4, and C16 showed consistently negative associations, while a chain-length-dependent pattern was observed: short-chain ACs were predominantly negatively associated, whereas most medium- and long-chain ACs reversed to positive associations in the second and third trimesters. Network topology analysis revealed stronger metabolite correlation structures in the heat-exposed group across all trimesters, with AA-AC pairs accounting for the largest proportion of differential correlations. Distributed lag nonlinear models suggested susceptible windows at gestational weeks 10–17 and 25–27 for AAs, and weeks 8–14 and 26–34 for ACs. Overall, prenatal heat exposure was significantly associated with multiple neonatal AAs and ACs, with distinct trimester-specific patterns and a denser intermetabolite correlation network in the heat-exposed group.

articles.title: Ecological Roles of Bacillus Lipopeptides in Mediating Plant–Microbe Interactions and Rhizosphere Community Dynamics
articles.abstract: Abstract The plant-beneficial bacterium Bacillus velezensis and related Bacillus species are increasingly recognized as important contributors to plant growth and health, yet the ecological functions of their secondary metabolites in situ remain poorly understood. Here, we investigated how lipopeptides produced by Bacillus species influence plant performance and root-associated microbial communities. Using Arabidopsis thaliana as a model host, we show that bacterial lipopeptides produced during root colonization promote plant growth by enhancing the uptake of essential mineral elements, including magnesium, calcium, iron, and zinc. Transcriptomic analyses revealed that lipopeptides upregulated host genes involved in metal transport and homeostasis in roots, while downregulating negative regulators of metal uptake. The lipopeptide production reshaped the composition of root-associated bacterial communities by increasing the relative abundance of putatively beneficial taxa and altering overall rhizosphere community structure. Functional genes indicated that lipopeptide enrichment was associated with microbial pathways related to metal transport, nutrient acquisition, and stress adaptation, suggesting that lipopeptides modulate both plant and microbial traits relevant to nutrient cycling. These results provide new insight into the ecological roles of B. velezensis-derived metabolites in plant-associated microbiomes and highlight lipopeptides as promising targets for harnessing beneficial plant–microbe interactions in sustainable agriculture.

articles.title:
Beyond Equilibrium:
Tracing Redox-Driven Pathways
That Shape Aqueous and Mineral Chemistry
articles.abstract: Abstract Numerous aqueous and geochemical systems host elements in multiple redox states, with wide ranging implications such as their influence on the formation/dissolution of minerals, water toxicity, and nutrient cycling. To uncover governing mechanisms and complex chemical interactions in geochemical systems, reactive-transport models have increasingly gained importance. However, their predictive capabilities remain limited because existing approaches struggle to accurately account for the full complexities of redox reactions. Here, we develop a reactive-transport framework that leverages recent advances in thermodynamic modeling, speciation chemistry, and redox kinetics. Distinct from traditional models, we uniquely treat redox kinetics along with transport as transient phenomena, decoupled from Gibbs free energy minimization. By ensuring ionic concentrations are governed by nonequilibrium rate laws, this approach allows predicting the tempo-spatial distribution of speciation and precipitation of species across oxidation states. We illustrate the versatility of our framework through two case studies: manganese speciation in natural waters and the fate of dissolved iron in aqueous/porous media. Our framework significantly enhances the modeling of a diverse range of redox-sensitive environments.

articles.title:
Receptor Binding
Drives Toxicokinetic Processes: Insights
from Two Amphipod Species Exposed to Insecticides Targeting the Nicotinic
Acetylcholine Receptor
articles.abstract: Abstract Insecticides targeting nicotinic acetylcholine receptors (nAChRs) are used because of their high neuroactive efficacy. However, they can also exert substantial toxic pressure on nontarget aquatic invertebrates. A previous study suggested that irreversible receptor binding is the main driver of thiacloprid bioaccumulation. To determine whether the observed elimination resistance applies to other nAChR-binding insecticides and species, this study investigates five compounds from different substance classes that target nAChRs. Using the two amphipod species, Hyalella azteca and Gammarus pulex, toxicokinetic experiments were combined with assessing receptor binding in vivo and in vitro. The three N-cyanoamidines and N-nitroguanidine neonicotinoids (thiacloprid, acetamiprid, and imidacloprid) and the metabolite imidacloprid-olefin showed resistance toward elimination (i.e., over 15 days of depuration in both amphipod species). This observation could be well described by a two-compartment toxicokinetic (TK)-receptor model (>0.89 R2) with integrated irreversible binding. In contrast, the butenolide flupyradifurone was fully eliminated, and the organic biocide spinosad was eliminated significantly but slowly, both fitted well with a one-compartment TK model (>0.71 R2). These findings demonstrate that receptor-binding specificity and affinity are highly compound class dependent. Although no direct link between receptor binding and acute toxicity could be established, elimination resistance indicates a risk for delayed, sublethal effects that should be critically considered in regulatory risk assessment.

articles.title:
Long-Term
Biogeochemical
Stabilization of Carbonate-Bearing
Pb–Zn–Cu Mine Tailings by Amendment-Assisted Phytostabilization
articles.abstract: Abstract Legacy Pb–Zn–Cu mine tailings can remain barren and geochemically reactive for decades. Although amendment-assisted revegetation can establish short-term plant growth, sustained phytostabilization requires metal attenuation and soil-like development over years after amendment-derived nutrients and organic matter decline. We evaluated seven-year biogeochemical stabilization of carbonate-bearing tailings planted with the native legume Dalea purpurea. Biosolids (BS), biochar (BC), and arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi (AMF) were incorporated into the upper 8 cm, while the underlying 12 cm remained unamended. Tailings pore water was monitored annually, and year-seven cores were analyzed by depth for organic carbon, PLFA-based microbial indicators, aqua-regia-extractable metals, sequential metal fractionation, and X-ray diffraction. Biosolids initially increased EC, DOC, DN, and dissolved Pb, Zn, and Cu, whereas BC- and/or AMF-containing treatments showed greater long-term reductions in dissolved metal concentrations. AMF-inoculated treatments increased organic carbon and microbial biomass indicators below the amended layer, while deeper root penetration was also observed, consistent with profile-scale biological development. Sequential extraction showed metal-specific repartitioning: Pb was primarily carbonate- and Fe/Mn oxide-associated; Zn remained partly carbonate-linked; and Cu shifted toward organic/sulfide-associated and residual pools, consistent with lower relative lability. These findings show that surface-applied amendment and planting strategies can promote coupled biological and geochemical stabilization in initially unamended deeper tailings layers, supporting ecosystem restoration beyond short-term surface revegetation.

articles.title:
Condensation Sink
Efficiency of Atmospheric Particles
Regulated by Their Chemical Compositions and Hygroscopicity
articles.abstract: Abstract Condensation sink (CS) from atmospheric pre-existing particles is a crucial limiting factor for the occurrence of new particle formation (NPF). However, intense NPF events occur frequently in polluted urban areas despite high CS levels. Here, to address this discrepancy, we introduce an efficiency coefficient ε (ε = CSeff/CScal) to quantify the CS efficiency of pre-existing particles toward gaseous H2SO4, where CScal was calculated under the assumption of irreversible uptake. Results demonstrate that ε strongly depends on hygroscopicity and chemical compositions of particles. Under dry conditions, the ε of pure organic particles was less than that of pure inorganic particles, but high humidity increased ε for both. For mixed organic-inorganic particles, the ε was adjusted together by particle chemical compositions and humidity. Exploratory measurements further revealed a decline in CS efficiency for gaseous HIO3. Incorporating ε into field data and models improves cluster survival predictions and sub-3-nm particle formation simulations, potentially explaining the NPF mystery in megacities under high CS and leading to more accurate modeling of NPF impacts.

articles.title:
Designing SynComs
for Resilience beyond Efficiency

Surface
Chemistry
Shapes Nanoplastic Mixture Responses
in Developing Amniote Embryos
articles.abstract: Abstract Nanoplastics (NPs) are an emerging environmental concern, yet their developmental impacts on terrestrial amniotes and their mixture effects are only beginning to be understood. Using a chicken embryo model, we compared the developmental and molecular effects of negatively charged (PS-COOH), positively charged (PS-NH2), and their equal-component mixture (50 nm). No significant mortality was observed across 0.1 to 10 ppm, whereas the lowest tested concentration (0.1 ppm) impaired growth and brain development without significantly increasing mortality. An IA-informed reference-response comparison showed that mixture effects were generally attenuated relative to reference responses derived from the experimentally tested single-particle treatments. Brain transcriptomic and proteomic analyses revealed distinct surface-chemistry-dependent responses: PS-COOH primarily affected extracellular matrix and glycan-related processes, whereas PS-NH2 altered synaptic, immune, and protein-quality-control pathways. The mixture induced the greatest number of DEGs; this broader omics response does not translate into higher phenotypic toxicity. DIABLO identified treatment-associated RNA-protein covariance, while reference-response comparisons indicated predominantly attenuated molecular responses among statistically supported deviations. Our findings demonstrate that coexposure to oppositely functionalized nanoplastics can reshape developmental and molecular responses during embryonic development.

articles.title:
Novel
Insight into Organoarsenic Degradation and Inorganic
Arsenic Sequestration in Ferrate Treatment: Unraveling the Role of
Active Fe–As Complexes at the Molecular Level
articles.abstract: Abstract Efficiently removing organoarsenic contaminants like p-Aminophenylarsonic acid (pASA) with their toxic inorganic byproducts remains a major challenge. Ferrate [Fe(VI)] can oxidize organoarsenic and immobilize inorganic arsenic, but the molecular mechanisms linking these functions are unclear. Here, using theoretical computational spectroscopy and stopped-flow analysis, we identified a critical pathway mediated by Fe(V/IV)–O-As(III) intermediates (INTs) that bridges oxidative degradation and heterogeneous sequestration. X-band EPR further confirmed the INTs (g-factors = 2.006, 1.928, 1.712), with rhombic peaks and quadruple hyperfine splitting. These INTs form barrierlessly between Fe(VI/V) and ·As(III)O(OH)2 released upon C–As bond cleavage in pASA. The thus-formed INTs exhibit superior reactivity to Fe(VI/V/IV), enabling more effective organoarsenic degradation and As(III) oxidation via outer-sphere electron transfer. Additionally, these INTs facilitate highly efficient inner-sphere electron transfer, forming Fe(III/II)–O-As(V) complexes that directly evolve into As-bearing Fe nanoparticles via Fe–O–As bond formation, a process with a lower energy barrier. The abundance of INTs during pASA degradation can be regulated by modulating Fe(VI) decomposition kinetics using common reagents: H2O2 accelerates and NaClO delays Fe(VI) decomposition. The Fe(VI)/NaClO system achieved 88% total As removal, higher than the 72% for Fe(VI)/H2O2 and 78% for Fe(VI) alone, and exhibited enhanced As–Fe coordination, indicating improved sequestration. Overall, this work reveals a pivotal mechanistic bridge in metalloid contaminant removal, offering new insights for designing oxidation-sequestration synergy in environmental remediation.
